outcome: optimal early feeding practice (defined as breastfeeding within one hour of birth and avoidance of prelacteal feeding in the first three days)
cohort: 5622 mothers who had a live birth in the two years before the 2014 Sudan Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey
finding: Only half of Sudanese mothers practiced optimal early feeding, and factors such as caesarean birth, birth at a health facility, maternal education, pregnancy intention, skilled birth attendant, infant sex, parity and maternal age were associated with early feeding practices.
mod_finding: Caesarean section was negatively associated with optimal early feeding practice.
